explain: A bounded selector chooses eligible passages without exceeding an already reserved evidence budget. This greedy heuristic is illustrative and may miss a better combination.
steps: Iterate passages in a declared priority order. || Add a passage only if its full rendered cost fits the remaining budget.
name: evidence-packing

explain: A controlled position experiment moves the same evidence to the start, middle, and end. It defines comparable requests but does not claim any particular model will fail in the middle.
steps: Keep the evidence and distractors fixed. || Construct three packets that vary only evidence position for later model evaluation.
name: position-probe

explain: Optimization is useful only under a quality constraint. A cheaper variant that fails the target is not chosen solely because it uses fewer tokens.
steps: Set the quality requirement before comparing variants. || Filter by quality, then choose cost among the eligible configurations.
name: quality-per-cost

explain: Release gates combine quality, critical invariants, and rollback readiness. A strong average score cannot override a permission violation.
steps: Record each mandatory release condition independently. || Block release if any critical condition fails.
name: release-gate
